summary: The move itself is clean and I verified it byte-for-byte: the only content change in either CommitLog.java or CommitLogTest.java is the package line. The nine re-recorded red records are genuine -- I re-applied three of the five mutations and got exactly the failures the backlog row claims, and each record's sha256 equals the sha256 of the staged test file, so the records bind to the bytes being committed. Re-recording was the right call over SKIP=check-tdd, and by a wider margin than the row realises. Two findings: (1) MAJOR, a rename blinds check-test-integrity completely -- I constructed the input it must reject (this same rename plus seven gutted assertions) in a throwaway worktree and the gate printed 'ok ... no test weakened' and exited 0; this commit is the first test-file rename in the repo, so the gate line the author is about to see is green having examined nothing, and the next move in M4 has no protection at all. (2) MINOR, a measured surviving mutation in the cost test. Neither requires a code or test change in this commit; the major's remedy is a backlog row (backlog.md is already staged) plus one sentence in the commit body, which preserves the pure-move property.

findings.title: A renamed test file is entirely unexamined by check-test-integrity, which then reports 'ok' -- and this commit is the first rename to exercise it
findings.failure_scenario: test_integrity.py builds its path list from `git diff --cached --name-only`. Rename detection is on by default, so an R099 rename emits ONLY the destination path -- I confirmed this: `git diff --cached --name-only` on the staged index lists sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLogTest.java and never lists the ingest path. For the destination, `before = git('show', 'HEAD:' + p)` returns None and the loop hits `continue  # new test file: nothing to weaken`. The source path is never in `paths`, so the removal side is never seen either. Net effect: every method in a moved test file is exempt from the weakened/removed/disabled check, and the gate prints 'ok no test weakened, disabled or removed alongside the production change'. I constructed the input the gate must reject rather than arguing it: in a detached worktree off HEAD I performed the identical rename of CommitLog.java and CommitLogTest.java, and in the same staged commit deleted six assertions (first.lastOffset isEqualTo(2), second.lastOffset isEqualTo(4), seen hasSize, seen.first isZero, seen.last isEqualTo(writers-1), sequences hasSize) and downgraded `assertThat(second.runs().get(0).firstOffset()).isEqualTo(3)` to `.isNotNull()`. git scored it R095, well clear of the 50% rename threshold. `python3 scripts/test_integrity.py <msg> ''` printed 'ok no test weakened, disabled or removed alongside the production change' and exited 0. The worktree was removed and the staged hash is unchanged. Concretely: an author can move a test file to a new package and gut every assertion in it in one commit, and check-test-integrity will pass, coverage will not move, and check-tdd will be satisfied -- because a gutted assertion is still falsifiable, so tdd-red.sh records a perfectly good red for it. Both halves of the harness that testing.md rules 2 and 4-5 rest on are blind at the same time, for the same input. This commit is clean only because the author diffed by hand and because I re-diffed HEAD:ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/CommitLogTest.java against :sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLogTest.java myself and found exactly one changed line. The next test-file move in M4 -- and M4 is a milestone whose whole shape is code moving into sequencer -- gets no such guarantee.
findings.remedy: No code or test change in this commit. Record the blind spot the way M0.17 and the check-tdd crash blind spot are recorded: a backlog row for teaching test_integrity.py (and tdd_scan.py) to follow renames -- `git diff --cached --name-status -M` gives source and destination, and the source blob is what `before` should be for a renamed path -- plus one sentence in the commit body saying that check-test-integrity's green line for this commit examined none of the nine moved tests, and that the pure-move claim rests on the byte diff instead. backlog.md is already staged, so this adds no code and leaves the move pure.

findings.title: committingCostsExactlyOneRequestWhenUncontended commits exactly once, so a per-commit request regression that only appears from the second commit onward survives the whole suite
findings.failure_scenario: Surviving mutation, measured rather than argued: delete `apply(delta);` from the success branch of CommitLog.commit (sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLog.java:134, inside `if (written.isPresent())`). I applied it, confirmed the class recompiled at the time of the run, and all 9 tests in CommitLogTest passed -- 'tests 9 failures 0'. The eight offset/sequence tests miss it because the retry branch, `apply(readDelta(keyFor(nextSequence)))`, self-heals the state on the very next commit: the second commit loses its race against the writer's own first delta, reads it back, folds the offsets in and succeeds at slot N+1 with exactly the offsets the assertions expect. concurrentWritersProduceOneUnbrokenOffsetSequence misses it because each of the eight writers gets its own CommitLog and performs exactly one commit. The cost test misses it because it performs exactly one commit, and the first commit is the one commit the mutation does not affect. I then measured what the mutation actually costs, driving CommitLog through CountingBinStore over three successive commits: unmutated the cumulative totals are 1, 2, 3 (one put each); mutated they are 1, 4, 7 -- commit 2 onward costs two putIfAbsent plus one get instead of one putIfAbsent, a 3x marginal request rate on the hot commit path. That is precisely the class of defect cost.md exists to forbid, and the test whose comment says 'ONE putIfAbsent for the whole flush ... neither scales with streams' cannot see it. Pre-existing: this holds identically on main today under binjava.ingest.CommitLogTest, and is not introduced by this change.
findings.remedy: Not in this commit -- adding a test would destroy the pure-move property that is the whole reason M4.2 is its own task. A backlog row: add a second `log.commit(...)` to committingCostsExactlyOneRequestWhenUncontended and assert `store.counts().puts()` is 2 and `store.counts().total()` is 2, which kills the mutation above. Verified the mutation is otherwise unkilled by the full CommitLogTest suite.

verified: PURE MOVE, byte-verified. `diff <(git show HEAD:ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/CommitLogTest.java) <(git show :sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLogTest.java)` yields exactly one hunk: `package binjava.ingest;` -> `package binjava.sequencer;`. Same for CommitLog.java. No assertion added, removed, reordered, renamed or loosened; no @Disabled; no comment changed.

RED RECORDS ARE GENUINE -- three of the five mutation groups re-executed independently. (a) Dropping the offset update inside apply() -- replacing `nextOffsets.merge(run.key(), run.lastOffset() + 1, Math::max)` with a no-op -- fails exactly five tests, and exactly the five the backlog row names: offsetsAreIndependentPerStream, aLostRaceRetriesAtTheNextSlotRatherThanFailing, recoveryRebuildsOffsetsFromTheLogAlone, offsetsAreMonotonicPerStreamAcrossFlushes, concurrentWritersProduceOneUnbrokenOffsetSequence. (b) Deleting the empty-commit guard fails anEmptyCommitIsRefused and only it, and it fails on the MESSAGE ('a delta with no runs commits nothing' where 'a commit with no runs' was expected) -- which independently confirms the claim in that test's own comment that asserting the exception type alone would have left CommitLog's guard deletable while the test stayed green. (c) A second putIfAbsent per commit fails committingCostsExactlyOneRequestWhenUncontended and only it.

RED RECORDS BIND TO THE COMMITTED BYTES. All nine binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest#* entries in .harness/tdd/red.json carry sha256 8261a00a4d24f91bf7982df4e2d1d78aa5156cbfe8b9fb556c080a8d32159b67, which equals the sha256 of the staged sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLogTest.java. Their `source` field is the new path. Timestamps run 08:16:03 to 08:17:17 today, four minutes after M4.1's commit at 08:12:21, and cluster five-within-six-seconds for the shared apply() mutation -- the shape of a real mutate-run-record session, not a batch forgery.

TREE RESTORED AFTER EVERY MUTATION. `git diff` is empty and `git diff --cached | sha256sum` is still ac6ec1dbce47dcc274bd767d7a6b78a627798cd36f9360e0e9ffef3b062d71fd. The verification worktree was created detached off HEAD under the session scratchpad and removed with `git worktree remove --force` plus `git worktree prune`; the staged index was never touched. :sequencer:test and :ingest:test are green against the restored tree.

SUITE COUNTS CONFIRMED from the JUnit XML: total 432 across eight modules (binstore-backends 86, binstore-spi 29, client 15, format 122, http 36, ingest 84, plugin 34, sequencer 26). The moved file contains exactly nine @Test methods, so ingest 93->84 and sequencer 17->26 is arithmetically sound and consistent with M4.1's recorded 432 total with sequencer at 17.

BACKLOG ROW'S ACCOUNT OF THE check-tdd EPISODE IS HONEST. tdd_scan.py keys ids as binjava.<pkg>.<Class>#<method> (scripts/tdd_scan.py:113 and :168) so the package rename makes all nine ids new, exactly as the row says. The nine original binjava.ingest.CommitLogTest#* records from M1.10 are indeed still present in red.json. One nuance the row does not mention and does not need to: the PATH change is independently sufficient -- tdd_scan.py's check() reads `HEAD:<destination path>`, which does not exist, so `before` is empty and every test in the file reads as new regardless of the FQN. Both routes lead to the same demand.

RE-RECORDING WAS THE RIGHT CALL over SKIP=check-tdd, and F1 sharpens the argument the row makes. The row justifies it as re-proving constraint, which is true. The stronger justification is that given F1, the nine red records are the ONLY mechanical evidence produced for these nine tests in this commit -- check-test-integrity examined none of them and will print 'ok' anyway. A skip would have left a moved test file certified by nothing but prose. Separately, the old records' `source` field points at a path this commit deletes, so they were about to become unverifiable against any tree. The one thing the row should not be read as claiming is that re-recording proves no weakening: it does not, because a gutted assertion still reds. The byte diff is what proves that, and I reproduced it.

NEW HOME IS APPROPRIATE, no misleading residue. No comment in the moved test refers to ingest; the class javadoc cites ADR-0002 and ADR-0001, both coordination concerns, and CommitLog's own javadoc cites the store-as-coordinator argument -- all of which read more naturally in sequencer than they did in ingest. concurrentWritersProduceOneUnbrokenOffsetSequence asserts I1 by a real eight-thread race rather than by the deterministic simulation sequencer/README.md promises, but that is not a gap this move creates: the retry-on-lost-race path it depends on is covered deterministically by aLostRaceRetriesAtTheNextSlotRatherThanFailing, and the simulation obligation is explicitly owned by M4.12 (fault-injecting store decorator and seeded harness) and M4.13 (1,000 seeds asserting I1-I5). Not a finding.

TIER IS RIGHT. All nine are T1 against MemoryBinStore, no clock, no socket, no system temp, no Thread.sleep, no fixed port, and CountingBinStore is a counting decorator over a fake rather than a mock. sequencer's new testImplementation(project(":binstore-backends")) is genuinely required -- MemoryBinStore lives in binstore-backends, while CountingBinStore is in binstore-spi which sequencer already had -- and testing.md rule 19b makes the request-count assertion backend-independent, so the dependency buys real assertion strength rather than convenience. The production surface stays binstore-spi + format.
